name: Joah
title: Scribe to King Hezekiah
summary: Joah, son of Asaph, served as scribe (mazkir/chancellor) under King Hezekiah of Judah. He was one of the three envoys sent to negotiate with the Assyrian commander Rabshakeh during Sennacherib's siege of Jerusalem. Joah played a crucial diplomatic role in one of the most critical periods in Judah's history.

keyEvents.title: Sent to Rabshakeh
keyEvents.description: King Hezekiah sent Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah out to the Assyrian commander Rabshakeh, who had come to Jerusalem with a large army.

keyEvents.title: Rabshakeh's Threats
keyEvents.description: Joah and the other envoys asked Rabshakeh to speak in Aramaic instead of Hebrew, so that the people on the wall would not understand the threats and become afraid.

keyEvents.title: Reporting to King Hezekiah
keyEvents.description: Joah and the other envoys tore their clothes in grief and returned to King Hezekiah to report what Rabshakeh had said.

keyEvents.title: The Crisis Leads to Prayer
keyEvents.description: After Joah and the others reported Rabshakeh's words, Hezekiah sent for the prophet Isaiah and asked him to pray on behalf of the people, which led to God's intervention.

keyEvents.title: God's Deliverance of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: As a result of the events in which Joah was involved, God intervened and struck down the Assyrian army, so that Jerusalem was saved from siege.
